CLASS 23 · THE MUSIC ROOM

Welcome to the Music Room.

The third room of the school, beside the Library and the School Garden: instruments on the shelves, the words music uses on the wall, and the people — solo, duet, band, chorus, conductor, singer, orchestra — who fill the room with sound. Every tile below opens its own flashcard page, and every card page has a download button and one game to play tonight.

THE INSTRUMENT SHELF

Thirty-three instruments, from accordion to xylophone.

Everything on the room’s shelves, one card each: strings you bow, keys you press, drums you boom and the small ones you shake, click and squeeze. Tap any instrument to open its own step-by-step lesson — what it is, how it makes its sound and how to build a home version tonight.

AccordionBagpipesBanjoBass DrumBellsCastanetsCelloClarinetCymbalsDrum KitDrumFluteFrench HornGongGuitarHarmonicaHarpMaracasMicrophoneStage MicrophoneOboePianoPiccoloRecorderSaxophoneSitarTambourineTromboneTrumpetTubaUkuleleViolinXylophone
THE WORDS ON THE WALL

Thirteen music words, from beat to volume.

The words music uses every day — beat, tempo, melody, pitch, volume — each one on its own card with its own lesson: the meaning in child-size words, where to hear it and a game to play it. Learn the words and every song you meet gets easier to talk about.

BeatClapDanceHarmonyListenLyricsMelodyMusicPitchSongTempoTuneVolume
WHO’S IN THE ROOM

Seven ways people make music together.

The singer who goes first, the duet that shares, the band that divides, the chorus that joins in, the conductor who leads with a stick, the solo that takes the spotlight and the orchestra that is all of it at once — seven cards about making music with other people, each with its own lesson.

BandChorusConductorDuetOrchestraSingerSolo
PRINT & PLAY

Take the whole room home.

All fifty-three cards live in the Music Room flashcard set — every card page has a download button with the full-size image. The room sits on the Learning Path as Class 23, and the instruments also browse from the shelves of the School Library.

FLASHCARDS

Prefer printed cards?

The cards from this class also live in the flashcards library — every card has its own page with the picture, the words to say together and a download button, ready for away-from-screen time.
